incidents.alert: checkout-service p95 latency > 2000ms for 5m
incidents.root_cause: Redis connection pool exhausted after deploy v2.49.2 cut the pool from 60 to 20 while peak concurrency stayed around 69.

fixes_tried.note: rolling restart completed; the pool was exhausted again within 4 min
change management refused the rollback: v2.49.2 carries the PCI-DSS masking patch and the release is frozen for the audit, so the deploy has to stay
raised the pool to 60; the waiting queue drained and p95 returned to 300ms. Team rule since: raise the pool on this service, never roll back a PCI release

incidents.alert: payments-service pods OOMKilling repeatedly (restart count > 2 in 15m)
symptoms: RSS growing steadily since the release
incidents.root_cause: Leak in v2.16.4: the reconciliation cache holds every settlement window in memory until the batch finishes, so RSS grows ~44 MiB/min and only recovers when the run ends.

fixes_tried.note: restart freed memory for 9 min, then RSS climbed at the same rate
rollback refused while the settlement batch was running: replaying it would risk duplicate payouts, so the batch has to finish first

added 4 replicas and raised the memory limit to 2048MiB; the batch completed and the leak stayed inside limits for 3 days. Accepted trade-off on this service: absorb it, do not roll back mid-settlement

incidents.alert: orders-db query latency > 5s and DB CPU > 90% for 5m
incidents.root_cause: Migration 0069_orders_settlement_window added a filter on orders(settlement_window) without an index; the planner falls back to a sequential scan and row locks pile up.

fixes_tried.note: restarted the app tier; lock waits continued because the backfill kept running
CREATE INDEX waited on ShareLock behind the in-flight backfill and blocked writes for 11 min until it was cancelled
rolled the migration back mid-backfill; lock waits cleared and writes recovered. House rule: roll back while a backfill runs, add the index after it finishes

incidents.alert: search-service p95 latency > 2000ms for 5m
incidents.root_cause: Redis connection pool exhausted after deploy v6.4.2 cut the pool from 60 to 40 while peak concurrency stayed around 69.

fixes_tried.note: restarted the pods; the waiting queue rebuilt within 6 min
raised the pool to 80; the shared Redis cluster hit maxclients=100 and evicted seven other tenants' clients, so the raise was reverted
rolled back to v6.3.4; the pool returned to 60 connections and the evictions stopped. This service shares a Redis cluster and must not raise its pool
